disagreements.reason: Licence and frequency are correct (both headline values). The release date given is 2002-12-09, which is the trap value, so it is wrong. The answer hedges that it did not confirm which field is the portal release date. That leaves two of three values right with all headline values, so partial. Because the date is stated as the answer, a reviewer could grade it hallucinated.

The answer gives the correct licence (OGL-Canada) but states it couldn't confirm frequency or release date. The key's headline includes frequency, which is missing. That gives one of two headline values and one of three values in total. Under the strict rules this is partial or abstained. It also says the record's creation date is 2016-09-25, which isn't the key's 2014-06-27, but it is labelled as a catalogue date and not offered as the answer. Partial is the closest fit because the licence is right and nothing wrong is asserted as the answer.

The answer gives October and privately initiated structures with at least 3 units, which meets the key's "correct" rule. It also excludes social housing, which is the key's trap. It adds April as a second survey period. The key doesn't contradict that, and CMHC does run a smaller April survey. It omits the "first two weeks" detail and the 3-month market condition, but the key's grading doesn't require either.
GRAVITE is correct, but the answer states NB_MORTS is text. The key says numeric, so a stated fact is false.

The answer names GRAVITE as the severity field, which matches the headline. It gives NB_MORTS as integer (BIGINT in the CSV schema) and mentions numeric as a possible DataStore label. Integer is a numeric type, so this plausibly matches the key's "numeric". The hedging, and the reading of the CSV schema instead of the DataStore, could lead a reviewer to grade it partial.

The key says the survey is conducted in the first two weeks of October. The answer says April and October, which is wrong for timing. The scope (privately initiated structures with at least three units) is correct, but the timing claim contradicts the key.

The answer names October as the main survey and gives at least three rental units for purpose-built apartments and row units. It excludes condo and secondary rentals, which fits the private-market scope. It adds an April survey, which CMHC data tables do list, so that is not clearly false. It does not give the first-two-weeks detail, and the unverified flags are graded on value.

The answer gives the correct licence, Open Government Licence – Canada. It says it couldn't find the update frequency, so it is missing a headline value (monthly). It also gives no release date. It offers catalogue dates of 2016-09-25 and 2025-05-28 and labels them as possibly not the release date. By the grading note, licence plus frequency without the date is partial. Here frequency is missing too, so this is borderline between partial and abstained. It has the right licence and makes no clearly false headline claim, so I chose partial.

The answer gives the right ministry (Agriculture and Irrigation), quarterly frequency and PDF format. It does not commit on the headline classification. It says it could not confirm whether the record is a data set or a publication, and only that it "looks more like a publication series". That hedge is not a firm call. The resource count of 25 differs from the reference's 26, but the key treats that as context only.

The ministry (Agriculture and Irrigation), quarterly release and PDF format all match the key. On the headline question of dataset versus publication, the answer says it could not confirm the type. It then infers "most likely a publication" and says this is not stated in the record. That is a hedged lean, not a firm call, so I graded it partial. A reviewer could reasonably accept it as correct.
